metadata.title: Why the Drug Reached the Tumor and the Tumor Still Grew Back
metadata.purpose: vox-explainer slate cut of Cancer Nanomedicine candidate 06. Source: cancer-nanomedicine/chapters/02-tumor-transport-barriers.md (outward interstitial fluid pressure mechanism and inside-out regrowth only).
metadata.color_semantics: TEAL = drug / particles accumulating at the rim; CRIMSON = unreached core / outward pressure / regrowth; GOLD = the pressure gradient highlight
metadata.note: EXCLUSIONS: diffusion limit derivation (1-2mm threshold), four-barrier list, 30-vs-150nm size debate, and radiation resistance. Keep ONLY: the outward-pressure mechanism (leaky vessels + no lymphatics -> fluid buildup -> net outward flow -> particles pushed back to rim) and the inside-out regrowth payoff (hypoxic core survives, selection for resistant cells, tumor regrows from core).

beats.narration_text: A nanoparticle drug reaches a mouse tumor. Leaky vessels — particles accumulate. The outer rim clears. Weeks later the tumor doubles in volume, growing from the inside out.

beats.narration_text: MRI at week three: a two-millimeter viable core. Whole-organ measurement confirmed drug accumulation. The core is untouched. The core then expands.

beats.narration_text: Drug reached the tumor. Vessels were leaky. Particles accumulated. Outer rim cleared. Weeks later the tumor regrows from the core. The drug was present. What kept it out of the core?

card.copy: The drug was present. What kept it out of the core?

beats.narration_text: The standard account: leaky vessels allow particle extravasation; particles then diffuse inward through tissue. That is accurate as far as it goes. The same leaky vessels produce a second effect that works against inward transport.

props.title: Leaky Vessels — Two Effects, Not One

items.label: Second effect
items.sub: Same leaks work against inward transport

production_viz.label: leaky vessels — two effects
production_viz.mechanic: one crimson vessel with two arrows: rightward TEAL arrow labeled EXTRAVASATION; leftward CRIMSON arrow labeled COUNTERFLOW
production_viz.note: the same anatomy produces both effects

beats.new_visual_element: [GRAPHIC] leaky vessel with paired arrows — in and out

beats.narration_text: Leaky vessel walls flood the tumor interstitium faster than lymphatics can drain it. Tumor lymphatics are absent or non-functional. Fluid accumulates. Interstitial pressure rises.

production_viz.label: in-flow > out-flow -> pressure
production_viz.mechanic: big blue inflow arrow entering tumor interstitium; small or missing drainage arrow; fluid gauge rises

beats.new_visual_element: [GRAPHIC] inflow >> outflow, interstitial pressure gauge climbs

beats.narration_text: Fluid flows down pressure gradients. The tumor core reaches pressures five to ten times above normal tissue. Net interstitial flow is outward — from the pressurized core toward the tumor periphery. A particle moving inward is moving against that current.

items.label: Core: 5–10× normal pressure
items.sub: Pressurized center; normal tissue at rim

items.label: Flow: core → rim
items.sub: Fluid runs down the pressure gradient

items.label: Inward particles fight the current
items.sub: Moving toward the core swims upstream

production_viz.label: outward radial flow
production_viz.mechanic: tumor cross-section with pressure gauge in core (5–10x) and rim (1x); radial CRIMSON arrows point outward from core; a small TEAL particle at rim tries to move inward against the flow
production_viz.note: keep radial symmetry; particle vs. current is the whole beat

beats.new_visual_element: [GRAPHIC] radial outward-flow arrows + one inward particle fighting the current

beats.narration_text: Particles extravasate near rim vessels. The outward current returns them to the periphery. They accumulate at the rim. The core remains particle-free — not because the extravasation mechanism failed, but because the pressure it created opposes inward transport.

props.title: Particles Pushed Back to the Rim

items.label: Core stays particle-free
items.sub: Not a failure — an opposing force

production_viz.label: particles pushed back to rim
production_viz.mechanic: tumor cross-section; TEAL particles enter at rim vessels; radial CRIMSON arrows carry them back outward; the core annotation reads UNREACHED
production_viz.note: extravasation succeeds AND fails at once — same mechanism, opposite outcomes

beats.new_visual_element: [GRAPHIC] particles enter → current returns them → rim accumulation, core empty

beats.narration_text: The unreached core is also hypoxic. Oxygen deprivation selects for cells with stress tolerance, suppressed apoptosis, and resistance to cytotoxic agents. The cells the drug never reached are not a random subset — they are the highest-resistance survivors.

props.title: The Hypoxic Core Selects for Resistance

items.label: Cytotoxic resistance
items.sub: Not a random subset — the survivors

production_viz.label: hypoxia selects for resistance
production_viz.mechanic: CRIMSON tumor core with low-O2 label; three chips fan out: stress tolerance, suppressed apoptosis, cytotoxic resistance
production_viz.note: the unreached cells are pre-selected survivors

beats.narration_text: The rim cells the drug killed were not the primary recurrence risk. The core cells it never reached were — and months of hypoxic pressure had further selected them for treatment resistance.

beats.narration_text: Illustrative scenario: a nanoparticle therapy reduces mouse tumor rim volume by sixty percent over three weeks. At week three, core IFP measures twenty-five millimeters of mercury; rim IFP: five. A viable two-millimeter core sits behind a pressure gradient the particles cannot cross. By week eight, tumor volume has doubled, originating from the core.

lines: Week 3: rim volume down 60%. Core IFP 25 mmHg; rim IFP 5.
A two-millimeter viable core sits behind the pressure gradient.
Week 8: tumor volume has doubled — originating from the core.

production_viz.label: illustrative — outward pressure, inside-out regrowth
production_viz.mechanic: timeline: WEEK 3 panel (rim shrunk, core intact, IFP 25 vs 5 chips), WEEK 8 panel (tumor doubled from center outward)

beats.new_visual_element: [GRAPHIC] two-panel timeline — week 3 vs week 8, illustrative numbers

beats.narration_text: Drug reached the tumor. The same leaky vessels that allowed accumulation flooded the interstitium and drove net outward flow. Particles remained at the rim. The core survived, selected for resistance, and drove recurrence. Accumulation was confirmed. Core delivery was not achieved.

card.copy: Accumulation is not delivery. Measure core IFP.
